description.value: Knight Inlet Lodge is an Indigenous-owned remote floating resort deep in the Great Bear Rainforest of British Columbia, owned by five partner First Nations and operated since the early 1990s. The lodge is accessible only by floatplane from Campbell River and offers multi-night grizzly bear viewing and whale watching packages in one of the last intact temperate rainforests on earth. Guest rooms feature queen beds, private en-suite bathrooms with heated floors, and views of the inlet, paired with fine West Coast seafood dining from locally harvested ingredients.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at grizzlytours.com clearly identifies this as Knight Inlet Lodge, an Indigenous-owned remote floating lodge accessible only by floatplane or sea in the Great Bear Rainforest. The site confirms active bookings for 2026 and 2027 seasons (May 21–October 15), establishing the business is open. No cycling-related amenities (bike storage, e-bike charging, tools, etc.) are mentioned anywhere on the site, which focuses exclusively on grizzly bear viewing and wildlife tours — all required_criteria and optional_amenities are null due to absence of evidence.
concerns: Lodge is accessible only by floatplane or boat — not reachable by bicycle. No cycling-specific amenities mentioned on site. OSM coordinates (lat 49.847, lon -125.133) place this in a remote inlet consistent with the website description, but no OSM tags or address data are available to cross-check.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, operating, publicly bookable accommodation confirmed open for 2026/2027 seasons; flagged always_include. Although fly-in access makes it atypical for cycling tourists, it is a legitimate destination and inclusion decisions are not the enrichment agent's role to override.
enrichment_extras.notes: Indigenous-owned (five First Nations partners). Seasonal operation May 21 to October 15. Small hydro-electric infrastructure with planned solar expansion mentioned for sustainability context.
